trigger: a packet 1.13 implementer reading ADR-0006 alone, which names four capacity signals but never obligates an alert
summary: The amendment says 'report' for charged bytes, headroom, oldest unexported age and refusals, but the alert obligation exists only in ADR-0075 R11.4 L645-646. Fix: add a 1.13 alert obligation to 0006. Page 1 is headroom below a threshold set above the refusal threshold. Page 2 is oldest unexported age held for less than the CH TTL minus the warm margin. Sustained refusals and a held capacity-unknown state get a ticket only. A single refusal or an over-size request never pages. Export headroom as a ratio with its denominator plus a capacity-unknown state. The alerts go in docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml with tests under the #2553 gate, using yuzu_ metric names and no per-run or per-agent labels. The reporter stated I5 and E0 for the whole report.
classification_rationale: A required operability obligation (alerting) is missing from the substrate ADR; nothing in it is contradicted.

trigger: a ClickHouse outage after the bulk-response cutover, with ClickHouse on the ordinary dispatch ingest path and no stated readiness posture
summary: The readiness posture is not stated (ties to SG-2). Recommend stating that ClickHouse is not a /readyz dependency, with the reason: including it would pull every replica out of rotation together. Use a degraded-state gauge plus the Page 2 alert instead. Bulk live responses make ClickHouse a hard dependency of the ordinary dispatch path, and 'never spill to PG' forces ingest to refuse or back-pressure. The ADR must say which ingest behaviour applies when ClickHouse is down and whether it affects readiness.
classification_rationale: The readiness and outage ingest behaviour is unspecified in the ADR text.

trigger: the export-dependent reap rule is enabled while ClickHouse holds the only copy of the record, with no backup or replication precondition
summary: The cold tier has no backup, restore or RPO/RTO. Once the warm copy is reaped, ClickHouse holds a single copy of the evidence. L155 gates the reap only on PG capacity, so a reaper could delete the last copy. Fix: state that ClickHouse backup, replication and RPO are a precondition to enabling the export-dependent reap rule; the numbers can come in 1.13. The ADR also does not define what ClickHouse 'export acknowledgement' means: a replicated insert or a node-local one. The reporter's stated impact (I5) is preserved.
classification_rationale: The backup/restore precondition and the acknowledgement definition are missing.

trigger: N core replicas each applying the recovery-throughput bound independently after an export outage
summary: Backoff and herd behaviour are named ('jitter', 'bound recovery throughput') but not specified. The text does not say whether the bound is per replica or fleet-wide; with N replicas it is per replica unless coordinated, and the same gap applies to export under C-4. A fleet-wide bound needs a PG-held lease or the leader gate (SRE-6). The ADR should state that the retry knobs are configurable and name the unit of the bound: rows/s, bytes/s or concurrent batches.
classification_rationale: The bound's scope, unit and configurability are unspecified.

trigger: packet 1.13 tries to declare the verification test passed against 'operating targets' that the ADR never defines
summary: The verification paragraph is not testable as written: 'within its operating targets' points at targets defined nowhere, and the reporter found no SLO in the ADR. Rewrite it as concrete pass criteria (ordinary-path p99 latency, WAL/disk, fleet-wide retry rate), with 1.13 supplying the numbers. Missing cases: ClickHouse flapping, a replica killed mid-reservation (UP-7), a mixed warm/cold aggregate during the outage (UP-12), partial acknowledgement, and a budget at the exact threshold edge (UP-9).
classification_rationale: Pass criteria and named failure cases are missing.

trigger: a new export loop added without a background_jobs.hpp HA class
summary: The HA classification of the export loop is not stated. background_jobs.hpp requires every singleton side-effecting job to declare a class. Recommend all-replica with idempotent per-batch claims (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) over FencedLeaderOnly, which adds a failover stall; if it is FencedLeaderOnly, it must fence the write, not a cached bool. The reap must be gated on confirmed export read from PG, not from a cache. The reporter named no line; the evidence is in server/core/src/background_jobs.hpp.
classification_rationale: The HA class and the reap-gate source are unspecified.

trigger: an implementer reading the ADR-0006 amendment on its own
summary: 'Retention deadline' is ambiguous and does not match R11.1/R11.4. Read literally, it means the 90-day cold retention, which would keep warm rows in PG for 90 days and defeat the capacity charge release at L160. R11 reaps on ttl_at (final + 20 min) plus exported_at. Fix: 'after the feature's warm expiry (ttl_at) and confirmed export', and say the 90 days is the cold TTL set by the feature. The reporter wrote 'I-low' (wrong reap timing, charge held longer) and derived MEDIUM; the recorder mapped that to I5 to match the reporter's band.
classification_rationale: Read literally, the Accepted ADR text conflicts with ADR-0075 R11.1/R11.4 reap semantics.

trigger: any creator read after warm expiry (the normal path)
summary: The authorization state a cold read checks after the reap is undefined. The warm read is owner-scoped via load_owned (R12.6), but gc_sweep deletes the result-set row, the only place the creator and owner are stored. Warm/cold read routing is also unstated. Fix: name in 0075 R11 the surviving authorization record (creator key, Forensics tier, device scope), where it is stored and who reads it, and add the rule 'warm if the row exists, else cold'. The reporter stated I4 and capped the band at MEDIUM because the gap is in a design doc. Derived from I4/E0 the band is HIGH, and the derived band governs the gate. The reporter folds this into SG-2/SG-3/AR-3.
classification_rationale: The surviving authorization anchor and the read-routing rule are missing.

trigger: an abandoned run, or an empty or excluded-only cohort, that produces no rows to export
summary: There is no release rule for a run that never reaches export. If exported_at is never set, the reap guard never fires and the reservation leaks slowly. Fix: stamp exported_at at final with zero batches for a run with nothing to export, and release the charge at reap for every terminal run. The reporter wrote 'I-low' (slow capacity leak, no disclosure) and derived LOW; the recorder mapped that to I8. The reporter stated no exposure.
classification_rationale: The release semantics for no-export runs are unspecified.

trigger: a reader treats the Accepted ADR-0006 amendment as decided approval of ClickHouse as the first durable destination for live responses
policy_floor: accepted ADR normative requirement: ADR-0006 L69-71 'one server substrate' (per-store engine choice rejected), contradicted with no supersession marker
summary: Table row 4 and the subsection 'Bulk live instruction responses (approved design, 2026-11-22)' make ClickHouse the standard first durable destination for live response payloads. That contradicts the amendment's own 'Migrating command responses requires its own response-store decision', ADR-0006 L69-71, and ADR-0075 R13.4 / packet 3C, and it goes beyond packet 1.1's scope. The same tension appears in 0039 L13-14. Fix: remove row 4 and the subsection and replace them with an out-of-scope sentence; in 0039 say the successor is 'proposed (ADR-0075 R13, D63), pending its own ADR'. The unconditional 'Never spill raw responses into PostgreSQL' contradicts the deployed store and resolves with the removal. The reporter gave no line or impact code; the impact is the recorder's derivation and the policy floor is the reporter's.
classification_rationale: Normative clauses in an Accepted ADR contradict each other.

trigger: a reader of ADR-0006 L72-75 alone, with no update banner pointing at the amendment
summary: The rejection clauses ('Per-store engine choice … Rejected'; 'ClickHouse remains the analytics sink … not the OLTP substrate') stand unqualified, and there is no top-of-file update banner like the existing 2026-11-14 one. Fix: add an update banner and an inline 'narrowed by Amendment (2026-11-21)' pointer at L69-75. The impact and exposure are recorder-derived; the reporter stated neither.
classification_rationale: The supersession signpost is missing from normative text.

trigger: a cold read while ClickHouse is unavailable, or a future feature adopting the exception
summary: The amendment's contract (row 2 and the 'A feature using the exception must specify…' list) does not say what happens when ClickHouse is unavailable. ADR-0007/0012 do say it for PG (fail closed). A cold read must not return an empty 200, which the reporter calls 'wrong-result no evidence (I3/I7)'. The boot posture is unstated, and the checklist omits deduplication and exact-count reads. Fix: add unavailability and read semantics (fail-closed retryable cold reads, boot posture) and a dedup/exact-read rule to the required elements, or assign both to packet 1.13. With I3 cited, the derived band is HIGH against the reporter's native MEDIUM.
classification_rationale: Unavailability semantics and dedup requirements are missing from the exception contract.

trigger: comparison of the 'PostgreSQL capacity during an export outage' section with R11.4 (D62)
summary: Three gaps against R11.4. R11.4 requires an alert where the amendment says only 'Report…'. R11.4 calls the never-fits case a permanent size-limit error, which the amendment does not mark non-retryable. R11.4 cites a general ADR-0006 cold-record capacity policy, but the section is written for criteria runs only. Fix: align the wording in one direction. The INFO note for 1.13: restart recovery needs a rule for reservations held by a dead replica, the export loop needs a background_job_class row, and 1.13's routed rows omit fenced leader election. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The wording diverges from R11.4 without a contract contradiction.

trigger: comparison of amendment row 2 with R11.3
summary: 'Core owns the credentials' is weaker than R11.3's 'only core holds the credentials', and row 1 does not say PostgreSQL stays the only substrate for transactional state. Fix: use R11.3's exclusive wording. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The weaker non-exclusive wording is not a contradiction.

trigger: new cold-store contract: packet 1.13 creates cold tables in the shared yuzu ClickHouse database with the existing credentials
summary: 'Grafana receives no datasource for these tables' cannot be enforced, because a ClickHouse datasource covers a connection, not a table. The datasource is defaultDatabase yuzu with no table scoping (deploy/docker/grafana/provisioning/datasources/clickhouse.yml:9-10). The shipped ClickHouse uses one default user with access management (deploy/docker/docker-compose.uat.yml:41-43). Core uses a single YUZU_CLICKHOUSE_USER/DATABASE (deploy/config/yuzu-server.env.example:87-90). Any Grafana Explore user could read per-device verdicts, and later Forensics-tier responses, bypassing R9/#4990. The responses row (:144) and the bulk section (:191) do not restate the exclusion. Fix: put cold-record and response tables in a separate database that only a core-only ClickHouse user can access, give the analytics/Grafana user no grant, add a deploy test, and apply this to the response tables. The reporter gave base HIGH; I1 with an E2 raise derives CRITICAL.
classification_rationale: The asserted control is contradicted by the shipped deploy configuration (false assurance).

trigger: new read path: a cold read after the warm reap while ClickHouse is unreachable or an RBAC read degrades
summary: The cold read's failure mode is not stated, and R11 is silent too. Fix: 'a cold read that cannot be completed is a retryable unavailable error (503 / MCP kInternalError), never empty or absent; an RBAC degrade denies (ADR-0041)'. I3 derives HIGH against the reporter's native MEDIUM. Because the status is speculative, it gates as a mandatory investigation. Owner: 1.13.
classification_rationale: The fail-closed semantics for cold reads are missing.

trigger: response successor contract
summary: 0006:191 and docs/adr/0039-response-store-postgres-migration.md:17 require Forensics-tier filtering. Neither carries #4990 clause 3: an unresolved tier fails closed (503, counted), never a partial 200, and a service-scoped token gets a definitive 403. Neither carries clause 1: the filter is pushed into the ClickHouse SQL, not applied to rows afterwards. The routed row still binds implementers. Fix: add these items to 0039's 'must specify' list. Owner: the packet 3C ADR.
classification_rationale: The #4990 clauses are absent from the successor requirements.

trigger: new data plane carrying per-device verdicts and Forensics responses over the plaintext http://clickhouse:8123 connection
summary: 'Core owns the credentials' says nothing about protecting them in transit or at rest (also :191). Fix: require TLS to ClickHouse for cold-record and response tables, with credentials from secret config and never in a PostgreSQL column (ADR-0010). Owner: 1.13.
classification_rationale: The transport and credential-protection requirements are missing.

trigger: a reader of the 'Considered and rejected' section who is not told the analytics-sink-only clause was narrowed
summary: The clause 'ClickHouse remains the analytics sink, fed separately; it is not the OLTP substrate' is not signposted as narrowed by the L132 amendment, which makes ClickHouse a cold store of record. ADR-0075 R11.3 expects the pointer. Fix: append a narrowed-by-Amendment (2026-11-21) note to L75 and add the same pointer to the top banner at L13. Owner: architect. The reporter cited I4/I7 and wrote MEDIUM; I4's base derives HIGH.
classification_rationale: The reporter classified this as an absent cross-reference in normative text.

trigger: front-matter related: lists only ADR-0035
summary: ADR-0075 and ADR-0039 are not linked from 0006's front matter. ADR-0039 never mentions ADR-0075, and its Parents line is unchanged. 0006 names ADR-0039 in plain text at L196 without a link. Fix: add 0075-criteria-runs and 0039-response-store-postgres-migration to related:, and link both on first mention. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The reporter classified this as wording (front-matter and links).

trigger: the sentence 'The implementing change enables that guarantee when cold export ships.'
summary: Ambiguous antecedent: 'that guarantee' could mean the capacity bound or the export-dependent reap rule. Fix: 'The implementing change enables the export-dependent reap rule, and with it the capacity guarantee above, when cold export ships.' The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: An ambiguous pronoun reference.

trigger: first-pass reading of L138-139 against the L144 row and the L187-196 subsection
summary: 'Migrating command responses requires its own response-store decision' reads as contradicting the later 'standard first durable destination' text; L195-196 reconciles them. Fix: add '(the destination is fixed below; cutover, rollback and historical reads need that decision)'. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The reporter classified this as wording tension that is reconciled later in the text.

trigger: packet 1.13 ships the cold store while data-architecture.md L40 still says ClickHouse is the analytics sink
summary: 'ClickHouse (below) remains the analytics sink…' will go stale at packet 1.13. It is not false today, and no routed row names the file, so this is a candidate rather than a required-doc obligation. 0006 L92-94 says data-architecture.md is 'updated to match this ADR'. Fix: carry it as a 1.13 doc obligation, or add the 0006-amendment clause now. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: A doc update will become due; the reporter says it is not an item-6 obligation.

trigger: data-store change plus a new system component that makes ClickHouse a core-credentialed store of record
summary: Evidence and system-description drift. The SOC 2 inventory lists ClickHouse only as 'Analytics events (sink-side) … Customer-controlled (external sink)', and docs/data-architecture.md:40 says ClickHouse remains the analytics sink. Both become false under the amendment. The Response store row (90 d) says 'MIGRATED TO POSTGRESQL (ADR-0039)' with no successor. Required-doc item 6: update the SOC 2 inventory and data-architecture.md in this packet, not 1.13, since ADR-0075 L928 already asserts SOC 2 scope. The reporter's status was 'unverified until packet 1.13' from reading and grepping the diff; recorded as likely. I7 is raised to HIGH because the omission conceals security-relevant behaviour, matching the reporter's HIGH (SOC 2 evidence integrity).
classification_rationale: Required-doc item 6: the inventory and boundary docs were not updated.

trigger: an auditor requests evidence for the 'core owns the credentials' and 'Grafana receives no datasource' controls
summary: The access contract cannot be evidenced. These are assertions with no named ClickHouse user, role or GRANT set and no artefact an auditor can pull; the repo's Grafana provisioning uses the default ClickHouse user. 1.1 requires a named dedicated ClickHouse user and role. 1.13 owes a periodic system.grants export folded into access-review evidence, plus a CI check that no provisioned datasource can reach the cold tables. This adds the SOC 2 angle to SG-1/SG-4. I6 is raised to HIGH as false assurance.
classification_rationale: The evidence-able control definition is missing.

trigger: ClickHouse designated store of record with no RPO/RTO, restore test or loss-disclosure rule
summary: Backup, restore and DR are missing; this overlaps C-2. ADR-0039 says only 'incomplete coverage after loss', which is a CC7.5/A1.2 gap once in scope. The amendment should either state a backup obligation for 1.13 or state that loss is tolerated and disclosed.
classification_rationale: The DR requirements are missing.

trigger: a ClickHouse TTL deletion or a warm reap happening with no disposal record
summary: Disposal and retention evidence is missing. ClickHouse TTL deletion is silent. The amendment states no cold retention period (90 d appears only in the inventory) and no disposal evidence. Required: a periodic, countable disposal record (one counts-only summary audit event per reap or TTL sweep, per R11.7), and the warm reap must be audited.
classification_rationale: Disposal evidence requirements are missing.

trigger: a cold read of Forensics (behavioural-PII) responses or of verdicts
summary: Cold-read audit is unstated; the amendment only says reads follow the feature's existing authorization rules. Forensics cold reads should be audited explicitly with rest_audit.hpp fail-closed semantics, and verdict-only reads need an explicit audit decision. SG-2/SG-3 cover authorization, not the audit trail.
classification_rationale: The audit requirement is missing.

trigger: a customer or auditor reading 'retained evidence' and 'store of record' literally
summary: 'Store of record' conflicts with 'not SOC 2 evidence'. R11.8 says verdicts are working data, not SOC 2 evidence, but the criteria-run paragraph calls them 'retained evidence'. Fix: call them 'retained records', cross-reference R11.8, and state that the SOC 2 evidence is the summary audit event (365 d floor). The cold store has no integrity or append-only guarantee and must not be offered as an audit-trail substitute. The impact is recorder-derived to match the reporter's MEDIUM.
classification_rationale: The amendment calls working verdicts evidence, conflicting with ADR-0075 R11.8 and the audit contract.

trigger: CC8.1 traceability review of 'Design approved by the platform owner on 2026-11-21'
summary: The approval line is a self-attestation that names no approver, no decision IDs (D27, D62, D63) and no link to ADR-0075 PR #8408. The 2026-11-22 subsection is dated differently from the 2026-11-21 amendment heading. Fix: name the approver, the decision IDs and the PR. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: Traceability references are missing.

trigger: an implementer reading the substrate ADR as authority
summary: 'permits the warm reaper to remove the records only after the retention deadline and confirmed export' reads as the 90-day cold period, given the 'cold retention period' usage at L145 and L136. That conflicts with ADR-0075 R11.1/R11.4 (ttl_at plus exported_at) and ADR-0072 L555. ADR-0006 is the bug because it is Accepted. Fix: 'only after the warm TTL (ttl_at) has passed and core has recorded the export as acknowledged (exported_at, HTTP 200 on every batch)'. The reporter stated E1 and wrote MEDIUM; I5 with an E1 raise derives HIGH. The reporter's 'I-capacity' (unbounded warm growth) is mapped to I5.
classification_rationale: The Accepted ADR wording contradicts the ADR-0075/0072 reap semantics.

trigger: loss of the ClickHouse volume while it holds the only copy of the cold rows
summary: L66-69 rejects polyglot persistence for 'a single HA story, a single backup story, and a single migration mechanism'. The amendment creates a second store of record without reconciling that, and with no ClickHouse backup, restore, replication or schema migration. A PG backup does not cover the cold rows, so losing the volume silently loses records of record. This is distinct from AR-1. Fix: scope the rejection to transactional state, and add backup, restore and migration to the per-feature checklist at L135-136. The reporter stated silent loss of records (I2) and wrote MEDIUM; I2 derives HIGH.
classification_rationale: ADR-0006 now contradicts its own rejection rationale.

trigger: reading which dispatch surfaces cut over, given that commands and instructions are separate surfaces
summary: The response scope is named four ways: 'Bulk live command responses' (L147), 'Bulk live instruction responses' (L183), 'bulk live response path' (0039 L14), and 'bulk live inputs/bulk responses' (0075 D63). Separately, L185-186 says ClickHouse 'is' the standard first durable destination, but today ClickHouseSink is a write-only analytics INSERT with no authenticated ingest or dedup token (server/core/src/analytics_sinks.cpp:38,:61). Fix: one term naming the surfaces, and 'will become … after the cutover'. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The reporter titled this a wording issue; it also covers present-tense phrasing that is ahead of the code.

trigger: comparison of the bulk subsection with ADR-0075 D63 (L756-760) under ADR-2002 multi-replica HA
summary: The bulk subsection is weaker than D63. It says 'account for bounded in-flight response bytes' and 'never spill', but omits that response capacity is reserved across all operators and replicas before fan-out and that a stalled sink pauses new waves. The criteria-run half says 'across all core replicas' (L159). Fix: 'reserve … across replicas; a stalled sink pauses new waves.' The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The reporter says ADR-0006 is wrong by omission.

trigger: three lists of successor-design requirements (0039 L15-17, 0006 L192, 0075 L765)
summary: ADR-0039 lacks rollback (which 0006 L192 has), and batch identity and durability (from 0075 L765 packet 3C) are missing from both ADRs. Fix: make ADR-0039's list the union of the three and have the other two point to it. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: Requirements are missing from the list that should be canonical.

trigger: a re-run more than 20 minutes after the run finishes (ordinary use)
summary: Re-run lineage is destroyed by the reap. gc_sweep runs DELETE FROM result_sets WHERE pinned=false AND ttl_at<$1. That removes source_payload (the input specs and digests R12.4/R12.7 need), cascades the members, and nulls the children's parent_id (:164). R11.1 forbids pinning and any second delete path. load_owned then returns not-found for a run whose cold record exists, so R8.4's whole-run re-run is unreachable and siblings lose lineage. Fix (1.1 text): name what survives the reap (e.g. a payload, owner and lineage stub outside gc_sweep), or state that re-run is warm-only. The exposure 'every run' is mapped by the recorder to E0 (scheduled sweep) and E3 (ordinary operator).
classification_rationale: The design does not say what survives the reap; this was verified against the code.

trigger: a cold read after the reap
summary: Cold reads have no authorization anchor. 'Same denial on the cold read' needs the owner, the cohort scope and the kind, and all three are in the deleted row. An implementation either fails open (no owner check: a cross-tenant read) or refuses every read. Fix (1.1): state that the authorization attributes are retained in PostgreSQL or exported with the records. The reporter stated no exposure code.
classification_rationale: The authorization anchor is unspecified.

trigger: async insert, or insert_quorum unset on a replicated table; the ClickHouse replica is lost after HTTP 200 and before replication, then the reap runs
summary: R11.4 treats HTTP 200 as durable and stamps exported_at on it. A 200 can mean the write reached only one replica's memory or local disk, and losing that replica after the reap loses the record for good (silent evidence loss). Fix: 1.1 names the acknowledgement contract (sync insert, quorum, or a read-back count) and 1.13 implements it. The reporter named R11.4 but no line.
classification_rationale: The durable-acknowledgement contract is undefined.

trigger: a long ClickHouse outage or a skewed ClickHouse clock, with partitions by day of final and a 90-day TTL
summary: The TTL can expire rows soon after export, so records never get their full 90 days, and a FINAL read returns empty rather than 'expired'. Fix (1.13): count the TTL from exported_at or a minimum retention date, with partitioning to match. The recorder derived I2 (early deletion) and I3 (empty presented as absent) from the reporter's text, giving HIGH against the native MEDIUM. Speculative status gates as an investigation.
classification_rationale: The retention-floor rule is unspecified.

trigger: an export retry after more inserts than replicated_deduplication_window
summary: The dedup window is finite: insert_deduplication_token is honoured only within replicated_deduplication_window, so a late retry writes the batch again. FINAL or GROUP BY hides this for exact reads, but not for aggregates or facets read without FINAL. Fix (1.13): every read path uses FINAL or GROUP BY; size the window to the backlog, or make dedup at the key the contract. The recorder derived I3 (wrong counts) from the reporter's text, giving HIGH against the native MEDIUM.
classification_rationale: The read-path dedup rule is unspecified.

trigger: batches 1..k get HTTP 200, then the core replica dies, or an upgrade changes the batch size or sort
summary: Partial batch acknowledgement plus a core crash. If per-batch progress is not durable, everything is re-sent and UP-5 applies. If it is durable, the batch cut must stay deterministic across releases, or an upgrade breaks the token mapping. Fix: 1.1 pins 'batch cut frozen per set version' and 1.13 implements it. The recorder derived I3 via the reporter's explicit link to UP-5's duplicate-write consequence, giving HIGH against the native MEDIUM.
classification_rationale: Batch-cut stability is unspecified.

trigger: a replica holding a reservation dies permanently
summary: 'Recover reservations after restart' assumes the same replica comes back. A replica that dies for good leaves its charge held, and admission stays refused (all retryable). Nothing requires an owner lease or epoch (WS-3). Fix (1.1): require reservations to be recoverable by any replica, via a lease or a reconciler; 1.13 implements it. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The reservation-reclaim rule is missing.

trigger: warm rows whose real footprint (TOAST, bloat, dead tuples before vacuum, WAL) exceeds the estimated reservation
summary: The capacity estimate can be too low: headroom is measured but the reservation is estimated, so PostgreSQL fills anyway and unrelated writes fail. Fix (1.13): use the measured relation size as a second gate. The recorder applies I5 raise (b), persistent exhaustion of the shared PG write path that audit and retention also use, to match the reporter's HIGH.
classification_rationale: A measured-size gate is missing from the capacity design.

trigger: headroom oscillating around a single recovery threshold with no hysteresis or dwell time
summary: The recovery threshold can flap, so admission oscillates and retrying clients form waves. Fix (1.1): add 'hysteresis band + jittered retry_after_ms'. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The hysteresis requirement is missing.

trigger: an operator REST delete of a run during an export or an outage
summary: The manual delete is guarded only by pinned=false, and runs are never pinned. It removes the only warm copy, and ClickHouse may keep unowned partial batches that a later read either can never reach or reads through no gate. Fix (1.1): define delete semantics for an unexported run; 1.13 implements them. The recorder derived I1 from the reporter's 'reads through no gate' branch, giving HIGH against the native MEDIUM; the reporter verified the delete path.
classification_rationale: Delete semantics for a set mid-export are undefined.

trigger: a release where R11.1's TTL reset lands before packet 1.13
summary: The reap guard is not yet in gc_sweep: today's predicate has no exported_at term. R11.9 discloses this, but having no release gate relies on documentation alone. Fix (1.13): add a test that pins the guard. The reporter rated it LOW because it is disclosed; the impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: A test pinning the guard is missing.

trigger: a count or aggregate over mixed warm and cold sets during a ClickHouse outage
summary: This extends SG-2 to aggregates; only the aggregate case is new. Such a count could silently skip the cold sets. Owner: 1.13. The impact is recorder-derived from 'silently skip'.
classification_rationale: Aggregate fail-closed semantics are unspecified.

trigger: a caller's device scope is narrowed after export, before a cold read
summary: RBAC can change between the warm and cold copies, and the text does not say whether scope is frozen at export or evaluated at read time. If the cold copy stores the scope at export, a later narrowing must still apply. This ties to UP-2. Fix (1.1): state 'read-time authority'. The impact is recorder-derived.
classification_rationale: The authority-timing rule is unspecified.

trigger: an upgrade with in-flight export batches from the earlier binary, or a ClickHouse table schema change
summary: 'Reconcile before opening admission' does not cover in-flight batches from the earlier binary or ClickHouse schema changes, so a mixed-version window can double-export or skip. Owner: 1.13. The recorder derived I2 (skip) and I3 (double-export) from the reporter's text, giving HIGH against the native MEDIUM. Speculative status gates as an investigation.
classification_rationale: The upgrade backlog handling is unspecified.

trigger: the response sink stalls during an incident-mode dispatch
summary: Under 'never spool to PG', buffer exhaustion means data loss. Incident mode raises the rate, so it reaches that point fastest, when completeness matters most. The amendment requires exposing coverage but sets no operator decision point (pause, or proceed lossy). Fix: 1.1 states the choice and 3C/3D implement it.
classification_rationale: The stall-behaviour decision is missing.

trigger: a run still gathering after deadline + warm TTL (R11.1) has passed, with export not started and the reaper looking only at exported_at
summary: Two state models conflict: walk status × export state × reservation × reap. One state is undefined, so a run that overruns its deadline before final could be reaped (I2) or held forever (I5). Fix (1.1): add a transition table. trigger: a customer architect or questionnaire responder quoting both ADR-0006 statements in diligence
summary: The ADR contradicts itself. L72-75 says ClickHouse 'remains the analytics sink… not the OLTP substrate', and the ADR says 'one server substrate… single backup story', yet the amendment makes ClickHouse a store of record. Fix: supersede or annotate the L72-75 rejection and the single HA/backup rationale, or cross-reference them.
classification_rationale: The reporter states the ADR contradicts itself.

trigger: a pilot deployment planning around the response cutover
summary: The ADR never states whether ClickHouse is mandatory; the 'cold tier on = required, stateful, SOC 2 scope' statement exists only in ADR-0075 L928. The bulk-response paragraph ('standard first durable destination', 'never spill raw responses into PostgreSQL') would make ClickHouse mandatory for every deployment after cutover, with no toggle. Fix: add one sentence saying the dependency is optional until a feature enables the cold tier, and that the response cutover must decide mandatory versus optional.
classification_rationale: The deployment-dependency statement is missing.

Fix: note that these responses are not updated until 1.13. 1.13 owes the whitepaper, shared-responsibility matrix, data-handling/DPA material, network flows and ports, and server-admin.md.

classification_rationale: This records future doc obligations; nothing is absent in this diff.

trigger: a 1.10-only pilot release, or incident mode advertised to a bank pilot, during a ClickHouse outage
summary: Rough edges for a pilot. In a 1.10-only release, evidence expires after the warm window with no export, and an operator may assume it is retained; the UI, the REST response and the manual should show the expiry. During a ClickHouse outage, incident-mode responses would be refused or lost under 'never spill to PostgreSQL', and the text does not say which. This overlaps AR-3/SG-2 and must be decided before incident mode is advertised.
classification_rationale: The pilot-visible behaviour statements are missing.
